title: Benchmark harness: explicit seed contracts, runner affinity metadata, and provenance export
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a provenance-first extension to the benchmark harness that (1) formalizes a seed contract for dataset and prompt sampling so generated profiles are reproducible across runner implementations, (2) attaches runner-affinity metadata to profile artifacts so the console/runtime can surface compatible serving variants, and (3) emits a compact provenance export alongside each published performance profile for auditability and regression debugging.
acceptance_criteria: A seed contract format defined (json schema) that encodes global RNG seeds, per-dataset sampling seeds, and deterministic prompt-variant selection rules
Harness produces identical profile artifacts when run with the same seed contract across Python and Go eval runners (byte-for-byte reproducible summary and stable prompt-sample lists)

Profile artifacts include runner_affinity field listing compatible runner tags (e.g., 'v2-kv-cache', 'quantized-8bit', 'gpu-tp-16') and a provenance.json that contains dataset SHAs, prompt generation rules, runner config hash, and Git commit refs
Console ingest pipeline can index runner_affinity and provenance fields (ingest tested via local staging)
Unit and integration tests cover seed contract edge cases (sharded datasets, streaming prompts, sampling-with-restart) with >90% deterministic rate in CI
Documentation (README + SDK snippets) describes how to pin runs using seed contracts and how to interpret provenance exports
tasks: Draft seed contract spec and JSON schema
Implement seed contract parser in harness core
Add seed propagation to dataset samplers and prompt generators
Extend eval runner shim to accept seed contract and emit sample manifest
Record runner configuration fingerprint and attach runner_affinity tags during profile publish
Produce provenance.json and attach to profile artifact bundle
Write CI tests validating cross-runner reproducibility
Console: add ingest mapping for runner_affinity and provenance fields
Docs: example workflows for stable onboarding & pinning
decisions: Use a single numeric master_seed plus per-dataset offsets rather than UUIDs to keep sampling deterministic across languages
Runner affinity tags will be additive labels computed from runner capability predicates (e.g., kernel set, quantization support) rather than exact version pins
Provenance will include Git SHA for harness and dataset, and a lightweight config hash for runtime settings to keep exports compact
tradeoffs: Master_seed + offsets simplifies determinism but requires careful handling for sharded/streaming datasets where order may differ across runners
Adding provenance increases artifact size and ingestion cost slightly, but materially improves debugging and regulatory audits
Runner affinity labels are conservative (may under-report compatible runners) to avoid serving regressions; this may delay automatic fallbacks
